item.title: LiteLLM Authentication Bypass via OIDC Userinfo Cache Key Collision (CVE-2026-35030)
item.description:

Tags authentication-bypass, litellm, oidc, jwt, cache-collision, ai-gateway, cwe-287
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System LiteLLM proxy (with enable_jwt_auth: true)
Versions Affected < 1.83.0
Language / Platform Python (target); Python PoC
Authentication Required No (unauthenticated attacker can hijack another user’s cached identity)
Network Access Required Yes (HTTP to LiteLLM proxy + attacker-controlled OIDC provider)

Summary

LiteLLM’s OIDC userinfo cache uses only the first 20 characters of the presented JWT (token[:20]) as its cache key. Two different, validly-signed JWTs can be crafted to share identical first-20-character prefixes, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to forge a token that collides with and inherits another user’s cached identity and permissions.
